faqs.q: How many Hz are in 1 MHz?
faqs.a: 1,000,000 Hz. Each metric step is ×1,000: 1 kHz = 1,000 Hz, 1 MHz = 1,000 kHz, 1 GHz = 1,000 MHz.
Common Wi-Fi bands are 2.4 GHz (2,400 MHz) and 5 GHz (5,000 MHz), with 6 GHz (6,000 MHz) on newer Wi-Fi 6E/7 routers.

faqs.q: What is the range of human hearing in Hz?
faqs.a: Roughly 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz) for young healthy ears. The upper limit falls with age - many adults top out near 15-17 kHz.

faqs.q: How do I convert frequency to wavelength?
faqs.a: Wavelength = wave speed ÷ frequency. For radio waves (speed of light ≈ 300,000,000 m/s), a 100 MHz signal has wavelength 300,000,000 ÷ 100,000,000 = 3 metres.

faqs.q: What does GHz mean for a processor?
faqs.a: Clock speed: billions of cycles per second. But GHz alone does not determine speed - architecture, core count and instructions-per-cycle matter as much or more.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Hz and kHz?
faqs.a: Just scale: 1 kHz = 1,000 Hz. Audio gear uses Hz/kHz, radio uses MHz, and processors and microwaves use GHz.
